text: Found it — lookupOrder does an exact-case match on order IDs, so the customer's lowercase "a-1001" fails to match "A-1001" in the data. The fix is to normalize the orderId with trim and uppercase before lookup; createRefund has the same case-sensitivity issue but isn't what was reported.
The lookup in `src/tools.ts` uses the raw `orderId` as an exact key, so a lowercase `a-1001` misses `A-1001`. I'll check the other callers and any normalization before concluding.

The root cause is that lookupOrder does an exact-case key match against ORDERS, so I need to normalize orderId by trimming and uppercasing it before the lookup. I'm also weighing whether createRefund in db.ts has the same exact-match flaw, since if the model passes a differently-cased orderId there, it could fail even after the lookup fix.

I'll keep the fix scoped to tools.ts since that's the root cause of the reported bug, though I can mention the refund path as a related concern. The fix works and type-checks. Writing `answer.json` to the project root now.

The root cause is in `src/tools.ts`: `lookupOrder` looks up the customer's raw order id as an exact key, so `a-1001` misses the stored `A-1001` and the model reports the order as not found. I changed the lookup to `ORDERS[orderId.trim().toUpperCase()] ?? null`. Before the fix, `A-1001` resolved and `a-1001` returned null. After it, both resolve to the shipped record, an unknown id still returns null, and `tsc --noEmit` passes.

`answer.json` is written to the project root. `package.json` and dependencies are unchanged.

The refund path has the same exact-case lookup: `createRefund` in `src/db.ts` indexes `ORDERS[orderId]` directly, so a lowercase id would throw "not found" there. I left it alone since it's outside this report, but it's a one-line fix if you want it.
